primary_method.name: DCF
primary_method.reasoning: KLA generates consistent, large free cash flows ($3.74B in FY25, $3.03B in FY24, $3.33B in FY23) through the full semiconductor cycle. It's a capital-light equipment company with capex averaging 2.5-3.0% of revenue. FCF conversion from operating income is high and predictable. DCF with a 10-year explicit growth phase through the AI capex cycle is the appropriate primary method. The cross-check is a peer P/E multiple on FY27E EPS given the market prices KLAC relative to the WFE equipment peer group.

wacc.reasoning: Beta 1.504 at a 4.3% risk-free rate and 5.5% equity risk premium implies equity cost of approximately 12.6%. KLA's process control monopoly characteristics, high recurring service revenue (estimated 20%+ of total), and 16-year dividend growth streak justify a quality discount to pure-beta. 9.5% WACC reflects this premium franchise adjustment. Net debt of $1.19B is negligible relative to $310B market cap; capital structure barely affects WACC.
wacc.adjudication_notes: Used 9.5% as base case WACC. Bear scenario uses 11.0% (closer to beta-implied rate, appropriate for a WFE down-cycle where KLA's cash flow volatility is higher than beta alone suggests). Bull scenario uses 9.0% (maximum quality premium; process control monopoly with 40%+ margins deserves the discount vs. a generic semiconductor company).

rf.reasoning: Risk-free rate, typically the local 10Y government bond yield. US ~4.4%, EM countries higher.

beta.reasoning: Equity beta vs local index. From yfinance unless sanitized to sector default.

erp.reasoning: Equity risk premium. DM ~5.5%, EM Indonesia ~6.5%, EM India ~6.5%.

debt_weight.reasoning: Debt portion of capital structure. Net debt / (net debt + market cap).

cost_of_debt_after_tax.reasoning: Post-tax cost of debt. Yield on outstanding bonds x (1 - tax rate).

terminal_growth.reasoning: 3.0% terminal growth for the base case. Semiconductor equipment is a secular growth industry tied to long-run expansion of chip manufacturing capacity; WFE is forecast to grow 7-10% CAGR through 2030 per SEMI consensus. Process control grows faster than total WFE as nodes advance. 3.0% is conservative relative to industry growth but appropriate for a terminal year assumption given cyclicality. It implies KLA's long-run growth converges to nominal GDP + ~0.5pp.

fcf_projections.rationale: FY26E (ending Jun 2026). Revenue at consensus $13.51B; FCF at 31% margin (consistent with FY23-FY25 average). Operating leverage modest as Gen-5 ramp adds some cost; FCF margin stable.

FY27E at consensus $17.0B (+25.8%). TSMC N2 volume ramp, HBM4 qualification, and advanced packaging inspection at scale. FCF margin expands slightly to 31% on operating leverage. This is the peak AI capex cycle year in the base case.

FY28E. AI capex cycle sustains but growth moderates from the FY27 peak. Intel 18A and Samsung 2nm contribute incremental volume. Advanced packaging inspection TAM growing. Revenue $19.5B at 15% growth vs. FY27.

FY29E. Post-peak normalization. WFE industry growth slows from AI cycle highs toward 8-10% as major fab buildouts complete. KLAC service revenue growing as installed base expands from the FY26-28 equipment shipments.

FY30E. Secular growth phase begins. WFE growth normalizes toward 6-8% annual rate. KLAC gains incremental packaging inspection share. Service base provides floor of roughly 20% of revenue regardless of equipment cycle.
FY31E. Continued secular expansion. EUV High-NA at TSMC and Intel drives next inspection intensity step-up. KLAC captures disproportionate share of the inspection TAM growth.
FY32E. Growth converging toward terminal rate. Revenue approaching $26B at 6% growth. FCF margin stable at 31%.
FY33E. Growth at 5% -- above GDP but WFE maturing. Service revenue at roughly $5-6B by this point provides stability.
FY34E. Growth decelerating toward terminal rate. Revenue at $28.9B. Minor margin compression as mix shifts toward lower-margin service.
FY35E terminal approach year. Growth at 3.1%, close to 3.0% terminal rate. FCF $9.23B. Terminal value applied from FY36.

wacc.formula: WACC = (1 - D/V) x Ke + (D/V) x Kd_after_tax;  Ke = Rf + Beta x ERP

explicit_fcf.formula: PV explicit FCF = sum( FCF_t / (1+WACC)^t ) for t = 1..N

terminal_value.formula: Terminal value = FCF_N x (1 + g_term) / (WACC - g_term);  PV TV = TV / (1+WACC)^N

bridge_to_implied_px.formula: Implied EV = PV explicit FCF + PV terminal;  Equity = EV - Net Debt;  Px = Equity / Shares

wacc_adjudication.notes: Used 9.5% as base case WACC. Bear scenario uses 11.0% (closer to beta-implied rate, appropriate for a WFE down-cycle where KLA's cash flow volatility is higher than beta alone suggests). Bull scenario uses 9.0% (maximum quality premium; process control monopoly with 40%+ margins deserves the discount vs. a generic semiconductor company).

cross_check.name: Multiple
cross_check.reasoning: Peer P/E multiple cross-check against the WFE equipment peer group (AMAT, ASML, LRCX, ONTO, NVMI). The market prices KLAC relative to this cohort; intrinsic DCF value understates market pricing because the 10-year explicit horizon still leaves significant franchise value in the terminal, and the market is paying a perpetuity multiple on a structural monopoly.

inputs.reasoning: Peer NTM P/E cohort: AMAT 34.9x, ASML 37.5x, LRCX 46.3x, ONTO 32.1x, NVMI 42.6x. Median is approximately 37.5x. KLA's 41% operating margin (vs. ASML 36%, LRCX 35%, AMAT 32%) and process control monopoly justify a 5-7% premium over the cohort median. Applied 40x to FY27E consensus EPS $5.05 = $202 implied price. This is the most relevant relative anchor given the market's framework for pricing WFE equipment.

scenarios.label: Bear
scenarios.probability_reasoning: 20% weight. A WFE down-cycle is the historical norm at 3-4 year cycle peaks. AI capex commitments are more visible than prior cycles, but TSMC capex cuts have happened before at similar points ($36B to $25B in FY23). China export control escalation is a binary risk with real probability. EPS beats contracting to near-zero is a near-term timing signal. The bear case is likely enough to size meaningfully, but AI infrastructure spending is more durable than historical WFE cycles.
scenarios.reasoning: TSMC cuts FY27 capex 20-30%, China legacy-node controls tighten, FY27 revenue misses at $14-15B, multiple de-rates to 30-33x.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.probability_reasoning: 35% weight. FY27E consensus $17B roughly plays out, with the multiple de-rating from 47x toward 40-43x as EPS beat rates stay narrow and AI capex narrative loses urgency. KLAC is a great company; the stock's issue is the entry point. Base case is the stock gravitates toward peer-relative fair value over 12 months.
scenarios.reasoning: FY27 consensus plays out at ~$17B; EPS $5.05 at 40-43x = $202-217. Stock trades down from $237 to the $200-215 range as multiple normalizes.

scenarios.label: Bull
scenarios.probability_reasoning: 15% weight. Bull case requires AI capex to extend beyond current consensus horizon, TSMC to maintain $40B+ capex through FY28, and the multiple to stay at 48-50x FY27E. Not the most likely outcome but materially possible: HBM4 + CoWoS + Intel 18A all materializing simultaneously plus FY27 beating $18B would validate this path.
scenarios.reasoning: AI capex cycle extends into FY28, FY27 beats $17.5B, EPS reaches $5.80+, market sustains 48-50x. Stock holds $260-290.

weights_reasoning: Scenario probabilities sum to 70% (Bear 20% + Base 35% + Bull 15%); cross-check gets 30% weight, totaling 100%. At $237, KLAC is priced well above even the bull DCF implied price (~$123 at 9.0% WACC / 4.0% terminal growth). The market prices KLAC on a forward P/E multiple basis -- the peer P/E cross-check ($202) is the most relevant fair-value anchor and deserves 30% weight because it directly reflects how the market will price the stock vs. AMAT, ASML, and LRCX. The DCF scenarios (70% combined) give the intrinsic value range ($37-123) and penalize the high-multiple current price. Bear 20%: real WFE cycle risk but AI capex more durable than prior cycles. Base 35%: most likely outcome; consensus plays out but multiple compresses. Bull 15%: real but minority-probability scenario requiring a perfect execution environment.
